subject: Mixed (Sample)
description: Sample questions only — for testing the app, not real exam content.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which muscle is primarily responsible for initiating abduction of the shoulder from 0-15 degrees?
questions.explanation: The supraspinatus initiates and assists the first 15 degrees of shoulder abduction before the deltoid takes over as the prime mover for the remainder of the range.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Normal adult blood pressure is generally considered to fall between which range?
questions.explanation: Normal adult blood pressure is typically cited as being between 95/60 and 140/90 mmHg; values above this range suggest hypertension.
questions.sourceBook: Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy
questions.question: In manual muscle testing, a grade of 3/5 (Fair) corresponds to which of the following?

options.B: Movement through full range against gravity, but no resistance tolerated
options.C: Movement through full range only with gravity eliminated
options.D: Full range against gravity with maximal resistance

questions.explanation: A grade of 3 (Fair) means the patient can move the part through the complete range of motion against gravity, but cannot hold against any added resistance.

questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics
questions.question: Which of the following is a distal realignment procedure used in the surgical management of patellar instability?

options.B: Patellar tendon transfer with tibial tubercle transfer

questions.explanation: Distal realignment procedures address patellar instability by relocating the tibial tubercle (with the attached patellar tendon), altering the pull line of the extensor mechanism. MPFL reconstruction (option A) is a proximal, not distal, procedure; C and D are non-surgical/rehabilitative measures.

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences
questions.question: In a patient with right hemiparesis following stroke, shoulder subluxation is best classified as which type of impairment?
questions.explanation: Shoulder subluxation arises secondary to the direct impairment (hemiparesis/hypotonicity) rather than being a direct consequence of the CNS lesion itself, so it is classified as an indirect impairment.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The anterior cruciate ligament primarily resists which movement of the tibia relative to the femur?
questions.explanation: The ACL is the primary restraint against anterior translation of the tibia on the femur.

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy
questions.question: TENS is primarily used in clinical practice for which purpose?
questions.explanation: Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) is primarily applied for pain modulation, commonly explained via gate control theory and endogenous opioid release.

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.question: The straight leg raise test is primarily used to assess irritation of which structure?
questions.explanation: The straight leg raise (SLR) test places tension on the sciatic nerve and lumbosacral nerve roots (typically L4-S1) and reproduces radicular symptoms when they are irritated, e.g. by disc herniation.

questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the cardinal signs of acute inflammation?
questions.explanation: The classical cardinal signs of acute inflammation are redness (rubor), heat (calor), swelling (tumor), pain (dolor), and loss of function (functio laesa). Necrosis is a form of cell death, not a cardinal sign of inflammation.

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health
questions.question: Screening asymptomatic individuals to detect a disease early is an example of which level of prevention?
questions.explanation: Secondary prevention involves early detection and prompt treatment of disease, typically through screening of asymptomatic individuals, to halt or slow progression.
